reactions.name: Formation of aminomethanol
reactions.description: Ammonia adds to formaldehyde to form the transient carbinolamine aminomethanol.

reactions.name: Formation of methanimine
reactions.description: Aminomethanol undergoes dehydration to produce methanimine.
reactions.conditions: Dehydration favored under suitable catalytic or water-removing conditions

reactions.name: Formation of aminoacetonitrile
reactions.description: Hydrogen cyanide supplies cyanide for addition to the imine, forming aminoacetonitrile.
reactions.conditions: Aqueous solution with available HCN/cyanide; pH-dependent

reactions.name: Hydrolysis to glycinamide
reactions.description: Hydrolysis of the nitrile functional group yields the corresponding amide, glycinamide.
reactions.conditions: Aqueous hydrolysis; heating and acid/base catalysis may facilitate the reaction

reactions.name: Formation of glycine
reactions.description: Hydrolysis of glycinamide produces glycine and releases ammonia.
reactions.conditions: Aqueous environment; usually requires suitable thermal and/or acid/base catalysis

net_reaction.description: The overall atom-balanced Strecker synthesis of glycine. Ammonia is consumed and regenerated in the simplified reaction sequence.

possible_environments: Meteorite parent bodies undergoing aqueous alteration
prebiotic_context.scientific_status: Chemically established Strecker reaction sequence and plausible prebiotic synthesis route; the complete sequence occurring under one specific early-Earth environment is not demonstrated.
limitations: Individual reactions are reversible or condition-dependent.
The aminomethanol intermediate can be short-lived.
Nitrile and amide hydrolysis may require heating or catalysis.
Competing reactions and formation of other organic products are possible.
